title: Three Dimensional Geometry: Direction Cosines, Lines, Angles and Shortest Distance
seo_title: Three Dimensional Geometry Class 12 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 11)
standard_text: Direction cosines and direction ratios of a line joining two points; Cartesian equation and vector equation of a line, skew lines, shortest distance between two lines; angle between two lines (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 12 Three Dimensional Geometry worksheet (NCERT Chapter 11): direction cosines and ratios, Cartesian and vector equations of a line, angle between lines, perpendicular lines, skew lines and shortest distance. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Direction cosines satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1.
body_html:
How it works

  • The line through (x1, y1, z1) and (x2, y2, z2) has direction ratios x2 − x1, …; divide by their root-sum-square to get direction cosines.
  • Line through a point with direction ratios a, b, c: (x − x1)/a = (y − y1)/b = (z − z1)/c, or r = a + λb.
  • Angle between lines: cos θ = |a1a2 + b1b2 + c1c2| ÷ (√(a1² + …) √(a2² + …)). Perpendicular when the sum is 0.
  • Skew lines neither meet nor are parallel. Their shortest distance is |(a2 − a1) · (b1 × b2)| ÷ |b1 × b2|.
Example

Find the direction cosines of the line through (−2, 4, −5) and (1, 2, 3).

Direction ratios 3, −2, 8

√(9 + 4 + 64) = √77

Answer: 3/√77, −2/√77, 8/√77

Common mistakes

  • Giving direction ratios when direction cosines are asked.
  • Swapping the point and the direction in the equation of a line.
  • Leaving out the division by |b₁ × b₂| in the shortest distance.

faq.q: What is the difference between direction ratios and direction cosines?
faq.a: Direction ratios are any numbers proportional to the direction cosines; direction cosines also satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1.

items.e: The line passes through (6, 5, −5) with direction −4î + 2ĵ + 5k̂: r = (6î + 5ĵ − 5k̂) + λ(−4î + 2ĵ + 5k̂).

items.q: Write the line (x + 6)/(−5) = (y − 1)/4 = (z − 2)/4 in vector form.
items.e: The line passes through (−6, 1, 2) with direction −5î + 4ĵ + 4k̂: r = (−6î + ĵ + 2k̂) + λ(−5î + 4ĵ + 4k̂).

items.q: Find k so that the lines (x − 1)/(−3) = (y − 4)/(−1) = (z − 3)/2 and (x − 1)/5 = (y − 2)/1 = (z + 1)/k are perpendicular.
items.e: Perpendicular lines: a1a2 + b1b2 + c1c2 = 0, so −16 + 2k = 0 and k = 8.

items.q: Write the line (x + 4)/(−2) = (y − 1)/(−3) = (z + 6)/2 in vector form.
items.e: The line passes through (−4, 1, −6) with direction −2î − 3ĵ + 2k̂: r = (−4î + ĵ − 6k̂) + λ(−2î − 3ĵ + 2k̂).

items.q: Find the Cartesian equation of the line through (3, −1, −6) and (8, 2, −8).
items.e: Direction ratios are Q − P = 5, 3, −2, so the line is (x − 3)/5 = (y + 1)/3 = (z + 6)/(−2).
